findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the prep cooler by the service counter to be holding time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods above 41F. The TCS foods stored in the cooler are listed below:
1. Ranch dressing (75F, probe)
2. Sriracha mayonnaise
3. Chipotle mayonnaise
4. Cut tomatoes (64F, probe)
5. Cheese (62F, probe)

All TCS foods in the cooler were stored there overnight. The staff were unable to provide a log of recorded temperature checks to confirm when the temperature in the cooler rose above 41F. All food items listed above were voluntarily discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the prep cooler by the service line fail to hold TCS foods at 41F or lower. The PIC stated that the cooler has been serviced recently. The ambient temperature of the kitchen was greater than 90F, with outdoor temperatures nearing 100F. Staff will use ice baths to hold TCS foods lower than 41F until the cooler is confirmed to be functioning. If the outdoor temperatures drop and the cooler is still not functioning, service will be required before the cooler can be returned to normal function. A follow-up will be conducted on September 7, 2026 to ensure the cooler is functioning properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple flies present in the kitchen during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that pest control professionals are routinely spraying the facility for pests, but the flies persist. The inspector recommends sealing any exterior openings, adding air curtains to exterior doors to prevent pests entering during food deliveries, and continuing pest control treatments on the facility. A follow-up will be conducted on October 2, 2026 to ensure the facility is free of pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the gaskets of the prep cooler and interior of the microwave to be soiled with debris. The PIC was informed that non-food contact surfaces are required to remain clean to sight and touch at all times. findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs stored above buttermilk and bleu cheese dressing in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was informed and the items were switched on the shelves. Ensure raw shell eggs are never stored above ready-to-eat (RTE) foods to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the dish machine to read 0ppm chlorine. The PIC was informed that the sanitizer concentration was low. The bucket containing the sanitizer was nearly empty. Facility was able to top off sanitizer bucket for the dish machine. The dish machine measured 150ppm chlorine following the repair. Ensure staff are checking the concentration of the dish machine with test strips frequently to avoid improper sanitization of dishes and equipment.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(A) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.

findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed food in the walk-in freezer to be stored on the floor. PIC was informed that all food items need to be stored at least 6 inches above the ground. This allows for proper cleaning and protects the food items from pests.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13  (C) Observed a bag of ground beef to be thawing in a sink full of standing water. Ground beef was immediately, voluntarily discarded. 
Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.152 - Several foods were observed without proper date marks, including but not necessarily limited to, boiled eggs and sliced tomatoes in the salad cooler, sauces in the top of the pizza cooler, open packages of sausage and pepperoni in the bottom of the pizza cooler, portions of deli meats, sliced tomatoes, and American cheese slices in the top of the prep cooler, noodles in the bottom of the prep cooler, and pulled pork and baked potatoes in the 3 door cooler. Benefit of the doubt was given for preparation dates. All foods were properly dated and kept for use. Owner and staff were advised date marking needs attention, and the practice needs major improvement. Foods that are not properly dated are subject to discard per inspector's discretion and may not be kept if a similar lack of date marking is observed at the next routine inspection.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous, ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.210 - Green beans in a hot holding well were observed to have an internal temperature of 127F-132F. Cook noted she reheated product in the microwave before placing it in the stream well. Temperature was not taken, and cook noted the container felt hot when removed from the microwave. Beans were being reheated and were placed back in the microwave to get temperature to 165F before being placed back in the hot holding unit for service. 

Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout the product. Properly reheat food to 165°F or above.
Always use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to check cooking and reheating temperatures to ensure foods are reaching proper temperature before being placed in the hot holding wells and/or before service. Make sure the hot holding unit is on in advance to help maintain proper hot holding temperature once products are placed in steam wells.

findings.comment:

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Bowl of lemons was observed in the ice bin at the wait station soda machine. Bowl of lemons was removed. Do not store general items inside the ice bins used to store ice for drinks.

B) Pizza crusts were observed unwrapped in the bottom of the pizza cooler. Some crusts were in direct contact with shelving. Proper covering and storage of foods between uses were discussed. Cover foods between uses and during long-term, overnight storage.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
750.290 - Ice scoop was observed with the handle down touching the ice in the bin at the wait station soda machine. Scoop was also observed to be soiled with soda splash along the handle. Scoop was removed and taken to dish area to go through ware washing.

Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - A) (R) Freezers were once again observed with heavy accumulation of ice/frost, most notably in the pizza freezer and the fry freezer. Defrost the freezers and maintain them clean.

B) (R) Bottom shelf of popcorn machine shelving unit was lined with foil. Remove the foil. Cease this practice. Obtain a smooth, cleanable liner (i.e. hard plastic, etc.).

C) Foil soiled with food debris and moisture was lining the metal shopping cart used for storage of sani-bucket and other items at the wait station. Remove the foil and provide a smooth, cleanable liner.
Owner noted a new stainless steel cart would soon be purchased to replace the metal shopping cart

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
Non-food contact surfaces clean
Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Clean pizza trays were observed between the wall and 3 part sink faucet. Cease the practice of storing cleaned/sanitized equipment in the area between the 3 part sink faucet and the wall. This area is subject to splash during ware washing.
 
Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Hot water handle was missing from the kitchen 3 part sink. A wrench was present to turn the water on and off at the hot water handle. Make proper repairs and provide a handle for the hot water at the 3 part sink.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors were soiled in the following areas:
A) BAR - 1. under ice bin at north end of bar (splash) &
2. under glass storage shelving at north end of bar (general debris);

B) KITCHEN - around the grease trap/under dirty dish shelving (food debris).
Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 & 1220 - A) BAR - Walls were soiled with splash under the ice bin at the north end of the bar. Clean the walls under the ice bin.

B) KITCHEN - Wall was damaged to the left of the stove. Repair the wall.

Walls must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.
